newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHILTON KEEPS CLEAN SHEET IN 1,000TH MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHILTON KEEPS CLEAN SHEET IN 1,000TH MATCH.

text.p: Peter Shilton celebrated his achievement in becoming the first player in English soccer history to clock up 1,000 league appearances by keeping a clean sheet on Sunday.
The 47-year-old former England goalkeeper who has performed at many of the world's great football venues, added another chapter to his remarkable career in a far from glamorous corner of East London.
A 10,000-strong crowd -- more than double Leyton Orient's normal crowd -- turned up to pay tribute to "Shilts" in the third division match against Brighton.
Orient won 2-0 with Shilton a spectator for much of the match.
A fanfare of trumpet players from the band of the Coldstream Guards marked Shilton's red carpet arrival for the kick-off.
As he trotted on to the pitch through a guard of honour formed by the other players and the match officials 1,000 balloons were released.
Shilton responded to the warm welcome by clapping his hands above his head as he turned to all parts of the ground.
First, Football League secretary David Dent handed the Orient goalkeeper a specially commissioned silver salver.
Orient chairman Barry Hearn followed with an award for Shilton's "outstanding achievement" to the game over 30 years.
Last up was a commemorative certificate from the Guinness Book of Records before Shilton jogged towards the goal he was to defend in the first half, once more acknowledging the applause.
Shilton admitted to some pre-match nerves after his 1,000th league appearance but said he was helped by the encouraging reaction of the crowd.
"It was not an easy game for a goalkeeper with nothing to do for the first 20 minutes...You just have to keep concentrating and obviously today it was a bigger task.
The fans have been absolutely superb. I did not really expect something like all this palaver. I just thought it would be a bit of a milestone but the fans were great."
Thoughts of retirement are still far from Shilton's mind.
"I will just get over today and keep playing. But I don't want to overstay my welcome," he said.
